title: Reference currents
note: What an interface may carry, from the cited documents (read 2026-10-07). The parts on a path (magnetics, connectors, fuses, ferrites) can allow less: record their datasheet ratings with set_part_rating and the sizing uses the weakest. null where no source could be confirmed.

rows.notes: 15.4 W at the PSE over Class D cabling, 13 W at the PD. The two wires of a pair share the pair current; a magnetics centre-tap trace carries all of it.

source.doc: IEEE 802.3 Working Group liaison to ISO/IEC SC25 WG3, 'IEEE P802.3bt Clause Referencing', approved 25 May 2017

rows.notes: 30 W at the PSE over Class D cabling, 25.5 W at the PD.

source.doc: IEEE 802.3 Working Group liaison to ISO/IEC SC25 WG3, 'IEEE P802.3bt Clause Referencing', approved 25 May 2017

rows.notes: 60 W at the PSE, 51 W at the PD. 4-pair figures are nominal to allow for current imbalance between pairs.

source.doc: IEEE 802.3 Working Group liaison to ISO/IEC SC25 WG3, 'IEEE P802.3bt Clause Referencing', approved 25 May 2017

rows.notes: 90 W at the PSE, 71.3 W at the PD (the letter predates the final standard). Siemon reports that the published 802.3bt table uses 0.96 A per pair for Type 4 (from a 100 VA limited power source); size for 0.96 A to be safe.

source.doc: IEEE 802.3 Working Group liaison (25 May 2017); Siemon, 'De-Mystifying Type 4 PoE Nominal Current Specifications'
